explanation: Write the product of values before each index, then multiply by a running product of values after it. This handles zeros without division.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n values. Two passes do constant work per position.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space excluding the O(n) result. Only the running product and indices are stored besides the result array.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 C++ algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: After the first pass, output[i] is the product strictly before i. During the reverse pass, the running product contains exactly the values strictly after i. Multiplying them excludes only nums[i], so each final entry has the required product without division.
walkthrough: For [3,0,-2,5], prefix products written to output are [1,3,0,0]. Multiply by suffix products [0,-10,5,1] at the corresponding positions, giving [0,-30,0,0]. Only the position containing the single zero has a nonzero result.
edgeCases: One zero leaves a possible nonzero product only at that zero’s position.
Two or more zeros make every output zero.
Negative factors keep their ordinary product sign.
